questions.question: A person invested Rs. 2,000 on simple interest for 7 years to obtain a total amount of Rs. 3,400 on a certain annual rate of interest. What was the rate of interest to obtain the above amount?
questions.questionHtml: A person invested Rs. 2,000 on simple interest for 7 years to obtain a total amount of Rs. 3,400 on a certain annual rate of interest. What was the rate of interest to obtain the above amount?
questions.solution:
Given:

The person invested Rs. 2,000 on simple interest for 7 years and obtain a total amount of Rs. 3,400 on a certain annual rate of interest.

Concept Used:

If P be the principal and r be the rate of interest then interest after t year will be (prt/100)

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Interest

Calculation:

Here,

Principal (P) = Rs. 2000

Time (t) = 7 years

Amount after 7 years (A) = 3400

Interest = A - P

⇒ 3400 - 2000

⇒ 1400

Let, the rate of interest be r%

Accordingly,

(2000 × r × 7)/100 = 1400

⇒ r = 10

∴ The rate of interest was 10%

Alternate Method SI in 7 years = 3400 - 2000 = 1400

∴ SI in 1 year = 1400/7 = 200

Rate(%) = \(\frac{SI}{P}\times100\) = \(\frac{200}{2000}\times100\) = 10 %

∴ The rate of interest was 10%

questions.question: Rs. 6000 is lent at the annual rate of 10 percent for 2 years. Which of the following is statement(s) is/are correct? I. Simple interest to be received on this sum is Rs. 1200 II. Compound Interest (compounding annually) to be received on this sum is Rs. 1260
questions.questionHtml:
Rs. 6000 is lent at the annual rate of 10 percent for 2 years. Which of the following is statement(s) is/are correct?

I. Simple interest to be received on this sum is Rs. 1200

II. Compound Interest (compounding annually) to be received on this sum is Rs. 1260

options.text: Both statement I and II are correct
options.html: Both statement I and II are correct

questions.solution:
I. Simple Interest = (P × R × t) / 100
⇒ (6000 × 10 × 2) / 100 = Rs. 1200

II. Compound Interest = P × [1 + (R/100)]t - P
⇒ 6000 × [(1 + (10/100))2 - 1] = 6000 × 0.21 = Rs. 1260

Hence, both statement I and statement II are correct.

questions.question: A man borrows a sum of Rs. 12,000 which amounts to Rs. 13,200 in 2 years on simple interest. What would have been the amount if the rate of interest was doubled?
questions.questionHtml: A man borrows a sum of Rs. 12,000 which amounts to Rs. 13,200 in 2 years on simple interest. What would have been the amount if the rate of interest was doubled?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Simple Interest is directly proportional to the rate of interest when Principal and Time are constant.

Original Simple Interest = Rs. 13,200 − Rs. 12,000 = Rs. 1,200

If the rate of interest is doubled, the Simple Interest will also be doubled.

New Simple Interest = 2 × 1,200 = Rs. 2,400

New Amount = Principal + New Interest = 12,000 + 2,400 = Rs. 14,400

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 14,400.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = Rs. 12,000

Amount in 2 years (A) = Rs. 13,200

Time (T) = 2 years

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (I) = A − P

I = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Calculation:

⇒ Original Interest = 13,200 − 12,000 = Rs. 1,200

⇒ 1,200 = (12,000 × R × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ 1,200 = 240 × R

⇒ R = 1,200 ÷ 240 = 5%

⇒ New Rate = 2 × 5% = 10%

⇒ New Interest = (12,000 × 10 × 2) ÷ 100 = Rs. 2,400

⇒ New Amount = 12,000 + 2,400 = Rs. 14,400

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 14,400.

Additional Information

Proportionality in Simple Interest

Simple interest is directly proportional to Principal (P), Rate (R), and Time (T). If any one of these is multiplied by a factor while the others remain constant, the Simple Interest is simply multiplied by the same factor.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the interest is calculated only on the original principal every year, meaning it remains constant per period. In Compound Interest, interest is calculated on both the original principal and the accumulated interest from previous periods.

Simple Interest Formula

The formula to calculate simple interest is I = (P × R × T) ÷ 100. The total amount at the end of the time period is the sum of the principal and the interest earned: A = P + I.

Total interest for 1 year in 2nd case = 12%

questions.questionHtml: Ram invested a certain sum of money at simple interest. It amounted to (5/4) of itself in 3 years. What will be its rate per cent per annum?
questions.solution:
Let Principal be P. Amount after 3 years = (5/4)P. SI = (5/4)P - P = P/4.

SI = P × R × 3 / 100. P/4 = P × R × 3 / 100.

1/4 = R × 3 / 100. ⇒ 100/4 = 3R. ⇒ 25 = 3R.

R = 25/3. R = 8.333%.

\([SI_{1} = \frac{P1 \times R \times T1}{100}]+ [SI_{2} = \frac{P2 \times R \times T2}{100}]\)  ⇒\([2000 = \frac{10000 \times R \times 2}{100} + \frac{5000 \times R \times 4}{100}] \)

questions.question: Rs. P are invested at 5% per annum of simple interest. After T years an interest of Rs. 82 is earned and the amount becomes Rs. 902. What is the value of T?

questions.solution:
Given:

Principal amount = Rs. P

Interest rate = 5% per annum

Interest earned = Rs. 82

Total amount = Rs. 902

Formula used:

Simple interest = (P x R x T)/100

Solution:

The interest earned is Rs. 82.

Amount = SI + P

902 = 82 + P

P = 820

The interest earned for T years

(820 x T x 5)/100 = 82

T = 10/5

T = 2

Therefore, the value of T is 2 years.

questions.question: A sum of money at a fixed rate of simple interest amounts to Rs. 1,630 in 3 years and to Rs. 1,708 in 4 years. Find the sum (in Rs.).
questions.questionHtml: A sum of money at a fixed rate of simple interest amounts to Rs. 1,630 in 3 years and to Rs. 1,708 in 4 years. Find the sum (in Rs.).
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Interest for 1 year = 1708 − 1630 = ₹78.

Interest for 3 years = 78 × 3 = ₹234.

Sum (Principal) = Amount after 3 years − Interest for 3 years = 1630 − 234 = ₹1396.

∴ The correct answer is ₹1396.

Alternate Method

Given:

Amount after 3 years (A3) = ₹1,630

Amount after 4 years (A4) = ₹1,708

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = Amount (A) − Principal (P)

In Simple Interest, the interest earned remains constant for every year.

Calculations:

⇒ Interest for 1 year = A4 − A3

⇒ Interest for 1 year = 1708 − 1630 = ₹78

⇒ Interest for 3 years = 78 × 3 = ₹234

⇒ Principal (P) = Amount after 3 years − Interest for 3 years

⇒ Principal (P) = 1630 − 234 = ₹1396

∴ The correct answer is ₹1396.

Additional Information

Simple Interest (SI) Formula

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is the Principal, R is the Rate of interest per annum, and T is the Time in years.

Rate of Interest Calculation

Rate (R) = (SI for 1 year ÷ Principal) × 100. In this case, R = (78 ÷ 1396) × 100 ≈ 5.58% per annum.

Constant Interest Property

Under Simple Interest, the interest added each year is always calculated on the original Principal, making the growth linear over time.

questions.question: Rs. 4,300 becomes Rs. 4,644 in 2 years at simple interest. Find the principle amount that will become Rs. 10,104 in 5 years at the same rate of interest
questions.questionHtml: Rs. 4,300 becomes Rs. 4,644 in 2 years at simple interest. Find the principle amount that will become Rs. 10,104 in 5 years at the same rate of interest
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Interest for 2 years = 4644 − 4300 = ₹344

Interest rate per year = (344 ÷ 2) ÷ 4300 × 100 = 4%

Total interest for 5 years = 4% × 5 = 20%

Amount = 100% + 20% = 120% of Principal

Principal = (10104 ÷ 120) × 100 = ₹8,420

∴ The correct answer is ₹8,420.

Alternate Method

Given:

First case: Principal (P1) = ₹4,300, Amount (A1) = ₹4,644, Time (T1) = 2 years.

Second case: Amount (A2) = ₹10,104, Time (T2) = 5 years, Rate (R) is same.

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI = P × [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100]

Calculations:

⇒ Interest (SI1) = A1 − P1 = 4644 − 4300 = ₹344

⇒ R = (SI1 × 100) ÷ (P1 × T1)

⇒ R = (344 × 100) ÷ (4300 × 2) = 344 ÷ 86 = 4%

⇒ Now for the second case, let the Principal be P2.

⇒ 10104 = P2 × [1 + (4 × 5) ÷ 100]

⇒ 10104 = P2 × [1 + 20 ÷ 100] = P2 × 1.2

⇒ P2 = 10104 ÷ 1.2 = 101040 ÷ 12

⇒ P2 = ₹8,420

∴ The correct answer is ₹8,420.

Additional Information

Simple Interest Property

In Simple Interest, the interest remains constant for every year as it is always calculated on the original Principal amount.

Effective Rate of Interest

The total interest percentage for 'T' years at 'R%' rate is simply (R × T)%. This is a very useful shortcut for solving Amount-related problems.

Relationship between A and P

Amount = Principal × [(100 + RT) ÷ 100]. This direct relation helps in finding the Principal when the Amount and Rate-Time product are known.

questions.question: A sum of money at simple interest amounts to ₹1,200 in 3 years and to ₹1,350 in 4 years. The sum is:
questions.questionHtml: A sum of money at simple interest amounts to ₹1,200 in 3 years and to ₹1,350 in 4 years. The sum is:
questions.solution:
S.I for 1 years = 1350 - 1200 = Rs.150

⇒ S.I for 3 years = 150 × 3 = Rs.450

∴ Principal,

⇒ P = 1200 - 450 = Rs.750

questions.question: A sum of ₹5,575 is invested at the rate of 8% simple interest per annum for 4 years. What will be the interest (in ₹) payable on maturity?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of ₹5,575 is invested at the rate of 8% simple interest per annum for 4 years. What will be the interest (in ₹) payable on maturity?
questions.solution:
Principal (P) = ₹5,575, Rate (R) = 8%, Time (T) = 4 years

SI = (P × R × T) / 100, SI = (5,575 × 32) / 100 = ₹1,784

questions.question: Rs. 5,000 is divided into two parts such that if one part is invested 4% and the other at 5%, then the whole annual interest from both the sums is Rs. 223. How much was invested at 4%?
questions.questionHtml: Rs. 5,000 is divided into two parts such that if one part is invested 4% and the other at 5%, then the whole annual interest from both the sums is Rs. 223. How much was invested at 4%?
questions.solution:
Let the 1st investment be Rs x so, the 2nd investment = Rs. (5000 - x)

x × 4/100 + (5000 - x) × 5/100 = 223 ⇒ 4x/100 + 250 - 5x/100 = 223 ⇒ 250 - 223 = 5x/100 - 4x/100 ⇒ 27 = x/100 ⇒ x = Rs. 2,700

questions.question: Suresh lent out a sum of money to Rakesh for 5 years at simple interest. At the end of 5 years, Rakesh paid 9/8 of the sum to suresh to clear out the amount. Find the rate of simple interest per annum.
questions.questionHtml: Suresh lent out a sum of money to Rakesh for 5 years at simple interest. At the end of 5 years, Rakesh paid 9/8 of the sum to suresh to clear out the amount. Find the rate of simple interest per annum.
questions.solution:
Given:

Total amount = 9/8 of the sum to suresh

Time = 5 year

Formula used:

Simple interest = (Principal amount × rate of interest × time)/100

Calculation:

Let the principal and rate of interest be P and R

Total amount = 9P/8

Simple interest = (9P/8) – P = P/8

S.I. = (P × R × T)/100

⇒ P/8 = (P × R × 5)/100

⇒ 1/8 = R/20

⇒ R = 20/8

⇒ R = 2.5%

∴ The rate of simple interest is 2.5%.

questions.question: An amount becomes double in 8 years on simple interest. In how many years would Rs. 25,000 become Rs. 1,00,000 with the same rate of interest?
questions.questionHtml: An amount becomes double in 8 years on simple interest. In how many years would Rs. 25,000 become Rs. 1,00,000 with the same rate of interest?
questions.solution:
Let, P = principal.

As per the question,

P = P × R × 8 / 100

R = 12.5%

Rs. 25,000 become Rs. 1,00,000 

So, simple interest is 100000 - 25000 = Rs 75000

So, as per the formula

75000 = 25000 × 12.5 × T / 100

T = 8 × 3 = 24 years

questions.question: If a sum of ₹5,000 is taken at a simple rate of interest of 15% per annum for 3 years and another sum of ₹8,000 is taken at a simple interest of 12% per annum for 4 years, the positive difference of the interests paid is:
questions.questionHtml: If a sum of ₹5,000 is taken at a simple rate of interest of 15% per annum for 3 years and another sum of ₹8,000 is taken at a simple interest of 12% per annum for 4 years, the positive difference of the interests paid is:
questions.solution:
SI₁ = 5000 × 15 × 3 / 100 = 2250

SI₂ = 8000 × 12 × 4 / 100 = 3840

Difference = |3840 - 2250| = 1590

questions.question: If the simple interest on Rs. 2,500 is more than the interest on Rs. 1,500 by Rs. 360 in 3 years. then find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.questionHtml: If the simple interest on Rs. 2,500 is more than the interest on Rs. 1,500 by Rs. 360 in 3 years. then find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.solution: SI = (Principal × Rate ×Time)/100 ⇒ 360 = ((2500 - 1500) × R × 3))/100 ⇒ R = 12%

questions.question: A man invested a sum of ₹5,000 on simple interest for 5 years such that the rate of interest for the first 2 years is 10% per annum, for the next 3 years it is 12% per annum How much interest (in ₹), will he earn at the end of 5 years?
questions.questionHtml: A man invested a sum of ₹5,000 on simple interest for 5 years such that the rate of interest for the first 2 years is 10% per annum, for the next 3 years it is 12% per annum How much interest (in ₹), will he earn at the end of 5 years?
questions.solution:
P = ₹5,000, t1 = 2 years, r1 = 10%, t2 = 3 years, r2 = 12%

SI1 = 5000 × (10 × 2)/100 = ₹1000

SI2 = 5000 × (12 × 3)/100 = ₹1800

Total Interest = SI1 + SI2 = ₹1000 + ₹1800 = ₹2800

questions.question: If the rate of simple interest in consecutive years is 4% and 5% respectively, then what will be the total amount payable on Rs. 25,000 in 2 years?
questions.questionHtml: If the rate of simple interest in consecutive years is 4% and 5% respectively, then what will be the total amount payable on Rs. 25,000 in 2 years?
questions.solution:
The SI for the first year:

⇒ (25000 × 4 × 1)/100 ⇒ 1000

The SI for the Second year:

⇒ (25000 × 5 × 1)/100 ⇒ 1250

Total Amount = 25000 + 1000 + 1250 = 27250
